The Tau Fitter solves a supervised classification problem, mapping coach-specific 4th-down choices to expected win probabilities. Its core failure mode is data leakage: using future seasons to inform current-period predictions breaks causality. The "wrong fit" stems from setting `point_in_time: false`, which pools all years into a single distribution, erasing temporal variance. To fix this, we implement a walk-forward window strategy, ensuring each prediction uses only strictly past data. This enforces temporal consistency and prevents silent degradation into league-average mediocrity. The resulting operator prices predictable coaching mistakes, such as punting when going for it maximizes win probability, before they occur.
